objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with chronic left shoulder pain without a history of trauma.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

“Hello, doctor. I’ve had a dull, gradually worsening pain in my left shoulder for about two months, especially when I move it to the extremes or use it a lot. It’s been disrupting my sleep and makes everyday things like brushing my hair and dressing difficult.”
Can you tell me your age, and

“Sure, doctor—I’m 55 years old. The pain has been going on for about two months and mainly bothers me when I move my left shoulder to extremes or use it, and it’s also been affecting my sleep and dressing.”
Have you noticed significant stiffness in the shoulder, as if

“Doctor, yes—there’s noticeable stiffness in the left shoulder, especially when I try to move it all the way or reach for things. It feels tighter at the extremes of motion and it’s made daily tasks like brushing my hair harder.”
Have you had any recent injuries to that shoulder, or do
“Doctor, no—I haven’t had any injuries or trauma to my left shoulder. I also don’t have neck pain or any numbness or weakness in my arm or hand.”
Do you have a history of diabetes or thyroid problems?
“Doctor, yes—I have type 2 diabetes, and I take metformin and glipizide. I don’t have any known thyroid problems.”
